{
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "taste_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.9,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "For food reviews, taste is a core product attribute and gives a strong axis to correlate with Score. Sample readings are sound (medicinal flavor -> poor, treat -> excellent). Slight risk of forcing a category when text is silent, but NULL handling exists."
    },
    {
      "name": "health_outcome",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
      "source_groundedness": 0.7,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "A genuine new axis for satisfaction analysis. However 'no_health_issues' is asserted for rows where health is never mentioned (dog food, taffy, delight confection), which is an unwarranted confident default rather than a silent NULL. This somewhat overstates groundedness."
    },
    {
      "name": "ingredient_transparency_trust",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.55,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Potentially useful attribute axis. But values are frequently invented: the mislabeled-peanuts row concerns labeling accuracy, not additives ('concerns_additives_mystery' is a misread), and the medicinal cherry soda text says nothing about additives. Values often not grounded in source."
    },
    {
      "name": "value_proposition_price_parity",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.8,
      "source_groundedness": 0.55,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Price/value is a relevant attribute. Grounded where text mentions price ('great price' -> good_value). But 'fair_price'/'good_value' is asserted for rows with no price mention (dog food, peanuts, cherry soda), a confident specific where text is silent."
    },
    {
      "name": "product_quality_verdict",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Well-grounded reading of reviews, but largely redundant with taste_quality and closely tracks Score itself, reducing its independent analytical leverage for this query."
    },
    {
      "name": "consistency_quality_control",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Consistency/QC is a legitimate attribute axis. Mislabeled peanuts -> defective is defensible. But 'consistent_reliable' is asserted broadly for silent rows (cherry soda, delight) without evidence, defaulting to a positive value."
    },
    {
      "name": "convenience_usability",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.5,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Convenience can matter for satisfaction, but most samples never discuss usability; 'convenient' is applied as an unsupported default, and 'inconvenient' for the peanuts row (a labeling issue) is a misread."
    },
    {
      "name": "intended_use_effectiveness",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.65,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Effectiveness-for-purpose is a useful attribute. Readings are mostly plausible (medicinal soda -> meets_purpose, mislabel -> use_case_mismatch), though 'effective_for_use' is sometimes a positive default on thin evidence."
    },
    {
      "name": "repeat_purchase_commitment",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.45,
      "source_groundedness": 0.55,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "A bare true/false flag that largely mirrors overall sentiment/Score, adding limited independent leverage. Also inferred confidently even when the review never states repurchase intent, so values are partly ungrounded."
    },
    {
      "name": "seller_recommendation_endorsement",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.5,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Endorsement is close to a positive/negative sentiment flag and heavily correlated with Score, limiting novel value. Some rows (delight, taffy) explicitly recommend, but many true/false assignments are inferred beyond the text."
    },
    {
      "name": "expectation_fulfillment",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.8,
      "source_groundedness": 0.75,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Expectation gap is a meaningful satisfaction driver distinct from raw quality. Readings are sound (not-as-advertised -> misleading_description, delight -> exceeds_expectations), with reasonable NULLs for silent rows."
    }
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.72,
  "source_groundedness": 0.66,
  "rationale": "The added columns collectively supply several genuine attribute axes (taste, expectation fulfillment, effectiveness, value, health) that give real leverage for correlating attributes with Score, beyond the original numeric fields. A few columns are near-restatements of overall sentiment/quality or the Score itself (product_quality_verdict, seller_recommendation_endorsement, repeat_purchase_commitment), lowering table-level usefulness. Groundedness is moderate: several columns assign confident positive defaults (e.g., 'no_health_issues', 'convenient', 'consistent_reliable', price values) to rows whose text is entirely silent on those aspects, and a few outright misread labeling issues as additive/convenience problems. This over-assertion, rather than using NULL for silent rows, is the main groundedness weakness."
}
